_what: #1329 B4m -- RECORDED INPUTS AND RECORDED VERDICTS of the S6I boots of 2026-09-11, so the launcher's arm/dry-run arithmetic can be replayed at the desk with no boot, no NVML and no CUDA. Every number below is quoted from a boot record or a boot log named in its own `source` field; nothing here is derived at the desk.

_sources.xsn13: /spinning/gpu-arb/weg2/BOOT_weg2xsn13_0911.md (48f55fb393, STOP at the dry-run, no card touched)
_sources.ring_source_boot: /spinning/evidence-665-f1/boot_weg2_weg2sn5b_d8ea6261f7_0909_185632.{front,P,D}.log -- the ring table's own source boot; ring_evidence/ holds ONLY the lines ring_table.solve parses out of them (WEG2-CHUNK-BYTES, WEG2-FLIP-TAG, KV Cache is allocated, the NVML->CUDA ordinal map, group P argv, WEG2-HOST-LEDGER CHOSEN, WEG2-CORRIDOR), plus the newest-per-group weg2sn5b samples of the host-ledger sidecar. 166 KB instead of 48 MB, and PROVEN equivalent: ring_table.solve returns byte-identical totals from this directory and from the full evidence dir.

cards_source: xsn14 front log, verbatim: 'NVML -> CUDA ordinal map: ordinal 0 = nvml 1 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 GPU-31d7ef41-f574-4d0e-21ad-e773fd938f6d total 32607 MiB, ordinal 1 = nvml 0 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 GPU-5c648f96-be1d-42d5-0221-34d11ab137f7 total 20480 MiB, ordinal 2 = nvml 2 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 GPU-62dbbae1-e859-9ccc-f9c2-d9f2443a84f4 total 20480 MiB'. THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: ring_table.solve maps list position to PP stage, so a card list in nvml order (0,1,2) instead of ordinal order (1,0,2) produces a different -- and silently wrong -- per-card H. Measured while building this fixture: nvml order gave total_h 55370055680, ordinal order gives the boot's own 46133149696.

ring_table.source: ring_bytes/ring_span1_bytes are the two fields of XSN13's own ValueError; ring_h_mib is XSN14's WEG2-XCHG-ARMED token 'ring_H_mib=43996'; the per-card rows are XSN14's three 'WEG2-HOST-LEDGER RING card=... H=... span1=...' L6 lines.
ring_table.no_form_gate_note: The SAME solve with p_argv=None, i.e. with the W48 FORM GATE UNARMED. Recorded because it is the only ring-solve answer that is HERMETIC: arming the form gate makes solve read the checkpoint headers of this boot's --model-path (planner/pp_cut.checkpoint_weight_terms globs *.safetensors and reads each shard's header), and that 27 GB directory exists only on the rig. Measured on the rig 2026-09-11: 46133149696 with the form gate armed (== the boot's own number), 46888124416 without. Both are pinned; the armed one only where the checkpoint lives.

checkpoint_dependency.read_by: python/sglang/srt/planner/pp_cut.py:2184 checkpoint_weight_terms -> glob *.safetensors, read each shard header
checkpoint_dependency.reached_from: ring_table.solve -> checkpoint_stage_weights (ring_table.py:802) when p_argv arms the W48 form gate
checkpoint_dependency.consequence: W48 Weg2RingFormMismatch on any box without the checkpoint. FOUND ON cachyllama 2026-09-11, not on the rig: the three form-gate tests failed there with "the checkpoint terms of '<model path>' could not be read". The replay is hermetic with respect to NVML, CUDA, /dev/shm and the boot -- but NOT with respect to the model directory, and that is now said out loud instead of being true only on one box.
checkpoint_dependency.owed: record checkpoint_weight_terms()'s OUTPUT as fixture data (its docstring says it measures headers, not bytes), which would make the armed-form-gate pin hermetic too. Needs one local run; deferred with the local execution slot.
